findings.contract: A ratio over two never-published custom metrics is admitted with exactly one returned expression. DescribeScalingPolicies preserves expression, labels, Sum/Average statistics and Count units, materializes outer CustomizedMetricSpecification.Dimensions and both nested Metric.Dimensions as empty arrays, and does not add query periods.

Managed ratio alarms use Metrics, not top-level MetricName/Namespace/Statistic/Unit/Period. Each source MetricStat gets Period 60; the expression query also gets Period 60. Alarm-level Dimensions is an empty array. High/low use 3/15 EvaluationPeriods and thresholds 10/9. DatapointsToAlarm and TreatMissingData are absent. Native alarm prose is not a contract.

Multiple returned series, all ReturnData false, expression and MetricStat on the same query, duplicate query IDs and missing expression references fail with HTTP 400 FailedResourceAccessException wrapping CloudWatch validation. Each failed update retains the entire previously described policy including configuration, ARN, CreationTime and alarm names.
A Metrics list mixed with single-metric Namespace/MetricName/Statistic/Unit/Dimensions fails with HTTP 400 ValidationException and leaves the existing policy unchanged.

Omitted expression ReturnData defaults to true and is materialized by DescribeScalingPolicies and managed alarms. Omitting a source ReturnData while the expression returns data, or omitting all ReturnData fields, fails with FailedResourceAccessException because more than one result is selected. These failures preserve the last successful policy. The successful omission update retains policy identity while replacing managed alarm names.

A simple custom metric with omitted Dimensions is admitted and DescribeScalingPolicies normalizes Dimensions to an empty array; explicit empty Dimensions yields the same metric specification. Managed alarms project single-metric fields at top level with Statistic Sum, Unit Count, Dimensions empty, Period 60, high/low EvaluationPeriods 3/15 and no Metrics member.
